canada.title: A day before US-brokered talks, Russia and Ukraine batter each other with long-range strikes
canada.summary: KYIV, Ukraine (AP) — Russia battered Ukraine’s power grid again and Ukrainian forces hit another of Russia’s biggest oil refineries, officials said Monday, hours before delegations from Moscow and Kyiv were due to meet for new U.S.-brokered talks on how to end the fighting.

canada.title: Decoding report card ‘edu-ese’: Why parents are frustrated and the province is getting involved
canada.summary: Alberta’s education minister has reopened the report card debate, proposing new legislation to make them more transparent for parents. Here’s what we learned by talking with parents and education experts about the issue.

canada.title: OSAP pause may force dental college to close, school says
canada.summary: An Ontario career college that has trained dental hygienists and dental assistants for 22 years may have to close as early as next month, due to a provincewide pause on student financial aid in the sector.

canada.title: B.C. lab ordered to pay $32K for misgendering transgender, non-binary patients
canada.summary: British Columbia’s human rights tribunal has ruled that a private laboratory provider must pay $32,000 in damages, along with other costs, for discriminating against transgender and non-binary patients.

canada.title: Parents warned extremist groups are targeting a growing number of kids online across Prairies
canada.summary: Violent extremist groups are grooming, recruiting and radicalizing a growing number of children and teenagers across the Prairies, police and researchers say.

canada.title: Tantramar Liberals oppose Holt’s Aulac toll plan
canada.summary: The Tantramar Liberal Association said in a Facebook post it is opposed to a provincial plan to charge a highway toll on New Brunswick's border with Nova Scotia. The association says tolls would negatively impact residents and businesses.

canada.title: Fredericton knitter uses yarn skills for international effort to save sea turtles
canada.summary: A Fredericton woman is one of six knitters chosen from around the world for a residency focused on sea turtle conservation.

canada.title: Is open drug use an issue in your town? Don’t expect police to make arrests
canada.summary: In many Nova Scotia communities, people are seeing more hard drugs being done out in the open. Police officials say a federal policy change is one reason the drug crisis is shifting dramatically, leaving officials with different ideas about how to tackle the situation on the ground.

canada.title: Future uncertain for Halifax home of Nova Scotia's first Black doctor
canada.summary: Community advocates are urging Halifax to preserve the historic North Street home of Dr. Clement Ligoure, Nova Scotia's first Black doctor, as the city acquires nearby properties to widen Robie Street for dedicated bus lanes.

canada.title: Behchokǫ̀ residents worry about health impacts of old uranium mine on Tłı̨chǫ lands
canada.summary: Multiple residents of Behchokǫ̀, N.W.T., say they are worried about the impact of a long-closed, but only recently remediated, uranium mine.

canada.title: Drug possession is illegal. Why can people use openly in public?
canada.summary: The drop in prosecutions — and the apparent rise in open usage — coincides with a Public Prosecution Service of Canada policy change in 2020 directing prosecutors away from laying criminal charges for drug possession, according to police officials and experts who spoke with CBC News.

canada.title: Artisans say they have a ‘fighting chance against AI’ at Craft Council fair
canada.summary: Quality is the name of the game at the Craft Council of Newfoundland and Labrador’s annual Christmas Craft Fair.

canada.title: These moms fought to change Canada's 'discriminatory' EI Act — and officially won
canada.summary: The legal battle is finally over for a group of six Quebec moms who fought to have certain provisions of the EI Act changed. The federal government says it will not challenge a Federal Court of Appeal ruling in favour of the mothers who were denied job loss benefits after their maternity leaves.

canada.title: Federal government commits $15.9M to National Field of Honour cemetery in Quebec
canada.summary: The federal government is preparing to take ownership of the National Field of Honour in Pointe-Claire, Que. The Last Post Fund has been managing the site for nearly a century, and say it's only cemetery in the country dedicated exclusively to Canadian veterans and their families.

canada.title: Devils’ Hellebuyck won’t play Tuesday in Winnipeg
canada.summary: Connor Hellebuyck will attempt to explain himself when he gets to Winnipeg.

lines: Good morning. I’m Hannah Thibedeau, and this is your Palindrome News brief.

Conservative Leader Pierre Poilievre is criticizing a key feature of the Carney government’s latest budget, arguing the proposed $15-million capital gains exemption on the sale of qualifying shares from a Canadian company applies too narrowly, excluding key businesses, CBC News reports.
A huge explosion and fire at an iron and steelworks in western Turkey left three people dead Monday as rescuers searched for 10 missing workers, officials said.
Trump says he was just kidding about making UFC’s Dana White his press secretary, The Associated Press reports.
Two trains collided Sunday south of the Egyptian capital of Cairo, killing seven people and injuring at least 125, authorities said.
Hakeem Jeffries says he’s a ‘hard yes’ on impeaching Pete Hegseth, NBC News reports.
That’s your brief. We’ll keep watching, so you don’t have to.
